newsitem.title: JAPAN: Iraqi crude imports to reach Japan in mid-February.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi crude imports to reach Japan in mid-February.

text.p: The first imports of Iraqi crude into Japan in almost six years are due to reach Japanese refineries in mid-February, oil firm spokesmen said on Friday.
Nippon Oil Co Ltd and Japan Energy Corp said loading of the Singapore-flagged tanker Maersk Navarin would take place in the Gulf port of Mina al-Bakr on January 20.

The very large crude carrier (VLCC) would deliver 1.1 million barrels to Nippon Oil's Negishi refinery in Yokohama and 700,000 barrels to Japan Energy's Chita refinery in Aichi, central Japan, spokesmen for the firms said.
The imports will be the first to Japan under Iraq's United Nations oil-for-food deal.

Under the plan implemented on December 10, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food and medicine for its people, who have been suffering under sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraq invaded Kuwait.
Mitsubishi Corp has signed a contract to buy 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraq's Basrah Light crude over a period of six months.
The major trading house is acting for five Japanese oil firms, including Nippon Oil and Japan Energy.
The other three refiners are Kashima Oil Co, Showa Shell Sekiyu KK and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
